_meta.project: instex Instrument Explorer -- IMAGER presets: the Palomar Observatory Sky Surveys on photographic plates with the Oschin 48-inch Schmidt (POSS-I 1949-1958, POSS-II 1985-2002) and their digitization at STScI (DSS-1, DSS-2)
_meta.companion: data/imaging/poss.md (same content as Markdown). Structure follows data/imaging/megacam_ztf_small.json: each parameter has value, unit, src (key into sources), loc, quote, optional alternatives / derived / note / check. The 'preset' object of each survey is the machine-readable summary for the explorer (a Schmidt telescope feeding ONE photographic plate: no pixels, no gaps; fineness from the emulsion and from the scan step).
_meta.rule: Every value carries src, loc and a short verbatim quote from a document saved unmodified under rawdata/imaging/poss/ (D20 is the ZTF paper already saved under rawdata/imaging/ztf/). DERIVED = arithmetic done here (shown). alternatives = other sourced values (conflicts). null = not published.
_meta.quote_check: All quote pieces (split on ' ... ') were machine-checked by script against: tesseract 5.5.1 OCR (pdftoppm 300 dpi greyscale, --psm 1) of the ADS scans (none has a usable text layer); pdftotext -layout and -raw of the arXiv PDFs; tag-stripped HTML; the FITS header cards of the DSS cutouts; the UTF-16 plate list decoded to UTF-8. Comparison removes whitespace and table separators, joins line-end hyphenation and normalises Unicode (NFKC), quotes, dashes, mu and degree glyphs; a few pieces match only after hyphens are dropped as well (check = 'loose'). OCR quotes keep the OCR's errors; each mangled number is flagged in a note and was read off the page image. Double-quoted fragments inside notes (OCR glosses such as "{/2.44", and FITS cards of the sibling headers) were checked the same way. Values marked IMAGE (R91 Fig. 1 band ranges, the wavelength range of R91's image-quality sentence) are not machine-checkable.
_meta.quote_check_result: 229 quote entries checked, 0 failures, 0 matched only loosely (hyphens dropped)

poss1.title: POSS-I: National Geographic Society - Palomar Observatory Sky Survey (48-inch Schmidt, original singlet corrector; 103a-O and 103a-E plates; 1949-1958) and its DSS-1 digitization
poss1.recommended_preset: Schmidt, plate at the prime focus inside the tube. D = 1.2573 m (49.5-in clear aperture at the corrector = the stop; H52), spherical mirror 1828.8 mm (72 in), R = 6125.5 mm (241.16 in), stop at the centre of curvature (D20). f_eff = 3070.0 mm DERIVED from the plate scale 67.187"/mm (H52; f/2.442, published f/2.44). eps NOT PUBLISHED (DERIVED lower bound 0.319 from the 14-inch plate; four vanes, D20). Detector: one 14 x 14 in (355.6 mm) glass plate, 1 mm thick, bent to the spherical focal surface (R ~ 3.07 m); 6.6 x 6.6 deg (43.56 deg2); unvignetted 5.4 deg diameter (field circle 324'; the mirror walk-off reproduces it, 5.34 deg). Bands: O = 103a-O unfiltered (lambda_eff ~4100 A, ~1100 A wide), E = 103a-E + red Plexiglas 2444 (6200-6700 A). Emulsion 80 lines/mm; smallest star images ~30 um (2.0"). Exposures 10-15 min (O), 40-60 min (E); limits O 21.1, E 20.0. Survey: 936 fields on a 6-deg grid (overlap >= 0.6 deg) to dec -33. DSS-1 (POSS-I E): 25.2845 um (1.70"/px), 14000 x 14000 px per plate; POSS-I O later at 15 um (1.0"/px, 23040 x 23040).

notes: Schmidt geometry for the drawing: corrector = stop at the mirror's centre of curvature, 6125 mm in front of the 1829 mm spherical mirror; the plate (bent to R ~ 3.07 m, concave toward the mirror) sits half-way, facing the mirror, in a plateholder carried by vanes from the ring girder. The mirror is oversized so that beams up to 2.67 deg off axis stay on it -- the same walk-off that the ZTF records describe (megacam_ztf_small.md, D20).

The plate replaces the CCD mosaic: one 355.6 mm (14 in) square of 1-mm glass, no pixels and no gaps. Its fineness: ~30 um smallest star images (2.0"), emulsion resolving power 80 lines/mm; digitized later at 25.28 um (1.70", DSS-1, E plates) or 15 um (1.0", O plates and 123 E plates).

MA63 (Minkowski & Abell 1963) is the standard POSS-I reference but has no ADS full text; every POSS-I number here comes from the documents listed above (H52 for the telescope; A58, A59, LD73 and R91, which summarises MA63, for the survey; L90, M00, L96, L08, the STScI pages and the DSS FITS headers for the scans).

poss2.title: POSS-II: Second Palomar Observatory Sky Survey (Oschin Schmidt with the 1985 achromatic doublet; IIIa-J, IIIa-F, IV-N plates; 1985-2002) and its DSS-2 digitization
poss2.recommended_preset: As POSS-I but with the 1985 Grubb Parsons achromatic doublet corrector (LLF6 + UBK7; < 0.5" images over 6.5 x 6.5 deg from 3900 to 9000 A). D = 1.2573 m (49.5 in; R91), f/2.44, 67.19"/mm -> f_eff = 3069.9 mm DERIVED; same mirror and stop; eps NOT PUBLISHED (>= 0.319 DERIVED). Plate: 14-in, 1-mm glass vacuum-held on mandrels reground to R = 120.9 in (3.07 m); filter in the plateholder. Bands: J = IIIa-J + GG395 (~4800 A), F = IIIa-F + RG610 (~6500 A), N = IV-N + RG9 (~8500 A). Emulsion 250 lines/mm; plates rejected if images exceed 40 um (3"). Exposures 50-70 (J), 70-90 (F), 90+ (N) min; limits B_J 22.5, R_F 20.8, I_N 19.5. Survey: 894 fields on a 5-deg grid, dec >= 0. DSS-2: 15 um (1.0"/px; header 15.0295 x 15.0), 23040 x 23040 px per plate, 42-um laser spot.

notes: What changed from POSS-I (R91 Sec. 3): an achromatic doublet corrector (1985) replaced the singlet plate; the plateholder mandrels were reground to R = 120.9 in and given a vacuum hold-down (+/-15 um); filters moved into the plateholders with nitrogen flushing; a stiffer defining frame (Oct 1989, flexure +/-5 um); an autoguider; a night-sky photometer and a 16-spot sensitometer. Emulsions went from 103a (80 lines/mm) to hypersensitized IIIa-J, IIIa-F and IV-N (250 lines/mm), three bands instead of two, 5-deg instead of 6-deg spacing, and dec >= 0 only. Mirror, aperture, f/2.44, plate scale and 14-inch plates are unchanged.

ZTF records that still apply (megacam_ztf_small.md, key D20): the 1828 mm spherical mirror, the stop at its centre of curvature 6124 mm away, the 3062 mm focal-surface radius, and the Grubb-Parsons doublet itself (ZTF adds a trim plate in front of it and a flattening cryostat window; its 1244.6 mm entrance pupil is a ZTF-era value).

The plate as detector: no pixels; the fineness is set by the emulsion (250 lines/mm = 4 um, 0.27"; star images <= 40 um = 2.7" on accepted plates) and by the scan (15 um = 1.0", with a 42 um laser spot).
